headline: Double-digit growth continues as margin and cash thin out
summary_short: StandardAero's Q1 FY2026 revenue rose 13.3% y/y to $1,626.9 million and net income grew 27.0% to $79.9 million, but Adjusted EBITDA margin slipped 130bp to 12.5% as mix shifted toward lower-margin platforms.
summary_long: Revenue grew across all three end markets — business aviation +19.6%, commercial aerospace +11.4%, military & helicopter +10.3% — led by the Engine Services segment (+14.1%) on a ramp in LEAP and CFM56 platforms. Cost of revenue rose faster than revenue on higher material costs from lower-margin platform mix, compressing Engine Services Adjusted EBITDA margin to 12.3% from 13.7%. Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 12.5% from 13.8%. SG&A rose 11.6% on bonuses and headcount. Operating cash flow used $119.6 million, versus $24.0 million a year ago, on a $249.0 million working-capital build tied to business growth. The company repurchased $60.1 million of stock and repaid $106.0 million of debt in the quarter; no forward guidance was disclosed.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by strong demand for services and products across all three major end markets, per the filing's own description of the quarter.
"Driven by strong demand for our services and products across all three major end markets," with business aviation the fastest grower.
Grew slower than revenue (+2.5% vs +13.3%) because higher material costs from a lower-margin platform mix outpaced the top-line gain.
Company attributes the increase to "higher material costs as a percentage of revenue" from increased sales of lower-margin platforms.
Reflects higher revenue and lower interest expense (weighted average rate 6.2% vs 7.1% a year ago), partly offset by higher income tax expense on higher pretax income.
EPS growth roughly tracked net income growth; diluted share count was nearly flat (333.4M vs 334.2M) despite the January 2026 GIC share repurchase.
Cash used in operations widened as net working capital grew, which the company attributes to "continued growth in the business."
Cash fell mainly on $60.1M of share repurchases and $106.0M of debt repayments, partially offset by $100.0M of new long-term debt proceeds.
Debt declined as $106.0M of repayments during the quarter outpaced $100.0M of new borrowings.
